entries.notes:
14x17 LW       SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to MCP at T7
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

Top of IR: 1.5-2” above shoulders
Collimation: 1" border around skin line

Position: Rest arms above head or hold bar (IV stand in front)

Notes: Left Lateral preferred

entries.title: CHEST: LATERAL DECUBITUS
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to GRID; 
       3" below jugular notch for AP;
       T7 for PA
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

Top of IR: 1.5-2” above shoulders
Collimation: 14x17

Position: 

Extend arms over head
Adjust thorax to true lateral
Elevate body 2-3" off table with sponge

Notes: Left lateral decubitus preferred

entries.title: C-Spine: AP ODONTOID (Open-Mouth) C1-C2
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 30" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; Enters midpoint of the open mouth
Breath: “AHH” softly during exposure (brings tongue down)

Collimation: 5x5

Position: 

Open mouth & adjust head so lower surface of upper incisors to tips of mastoid ⟂ to IR
Mouth open as wide as possible
(Shows Atlas: C1 & Axis: C2)

entries.title: C-Spine: AP AXIAL OBLIQUE (LPO/RPO)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: 15-20° cephalad, directed to C4 
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 10x12 
IR: Centered to C3 body
      1" superior to most prominent point of thyroid cartilage

Position: 

Rotate shoulders 45° & center to cervical spine to IR
Elevate & protrude chin
(Shows intervertebral foramina and pedicles farthest from the IR)

Notes: LPO = right foramina | RPO = left foramina

entries.title: C-Spine: LATERAL (GRANDY)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to MCP at C4
Breath: Suspend at end of full expiration

Collimation: 10x12 
Top of IR: 1” above top of EAM
  
Position: 

Sandbags to patient's wrists to depress shoulders (to get C7)
C4 in center
Elevate chin slightly, mandible protruded
(Shows vertebral bodies, zygapophyseal joints, & open intervertebral disk spaces)

Notes: *If cervical spine trauma is suspected, this projection must be performed first and *cleared* by radiologist before additional images are performed.
*If top third of T1 is not demonstrated, lateral of cervicothoracic is required (Swimmers).

entries.title: C-Spine: AP DENS (FUCHS)
entries.notes:
10x12 CW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; Enters the neck on the MSP just distal to the tip of the chin
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 5x5

Position: 

Center the IR to the level of the tips of the mastoid processes
Extend the chin until the tip of the chin and the tips of the mastoid process are vertical
(Shows dens within the foramen magnum)

Notes: Fuchs method is contraindicated if cervical fracture or disease is suspected.

entries.title: C-Spine: LATERAL - Hyperflexion & Hyperextension
tags: hyperextension; c-spine lateral hyperextension; c-spine lateral hyperflexion
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to C4
Breath: Suspend 

Collimation: 10x12 
Top of IR: 1” above top of EAM
  
Position: 

Same as for lateral (Grandy)
Hyperflexion: Have patient drop head forward and draw the chin as close as possible to chest; Body of the mandible almost vertical

Hyperextension: Have patient elevate chin and relax head as far back as possible; Body of the mandible almost horizontal

Elevate chin slightly, mandible protruded
(Checks for absent motion from trauma/disease)

Notes: *Used to demonstrate absence of normal movement from trauma or disease.
*This procedure must not be attempted until cervical spine pathology or fracture has been ruled out.

entries.title: C-Spine: PA AXIAL OBLIQUE (RAO/LAO) *preferred*
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: 15-20° caudad, at C4 
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 10x12 
IR: Centered to C5 body
      1" caudal to most prominent point of thyroid cartilage

Position: 

Rotate body & neck 45° 
Elevate & protrude chin
(Shows RAO/LAO = Intervertebral foramina and pedicles closest to the IR)

Notes: RAO = right foramina | LAO = left foramina

entries.title: T-Spine: AP
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; ½ between jugular notch & xiphoid (T7)
Breath: Suspend at expiration

Collimation: 7x17
Top of IR: 1.5-2” above shoulders (this places T7 in center) 

Position: 
If supine, reduce kyphosis by flexing hips and knees to place thighs vertical
If upright, weight should be equally distributed on both feet
(Shows costovertebral articulations)

Notes: If possible, orient patient so lower thorax is at cathode end of x-ray tube. This orientation takes advantage of the “anode heel effect” to ensure a more uniform exposure of the thoracic anatomy.

entries.title: SCOLIOSIS: LATERAL ThoracoLumbar Spine
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40-72”
CR: ⟂ to IR

Centering points for each sequence will be dictated by the system used
A two (or three) image sequence is performed 
Breath: Suspend 

Collimation: varies

Position: 
Arms at right angle to body or upward 
Position special ruler adjacent to spine, if needed
(shows entire spine from base of skull to tip of coccyx)

entries.title: CervicoThoracic Spine: LATERAL (SWIMMERS)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40"
CR: ⟂ to C7-T1 interspace (if shoulder away from IR is depressed)
If shoulder cannot be depressed, angle 3 to 5° caudad (to better visualize the C7-T1 articulation)
Breath: Suspend or use a breathing technique (to blur lung anatomy)

Collimation: 10x12
Top of IR: 1.5-2” above relaxed shoulders

Position: 

Extend arm closer to IR above head, and rotate humeral head anteriorly (If upright, flex elbow, and rest forearm on head)
Depress shoulder farther from IR (If possible, rotate humeral head in the opposite direction to the other shoulder)
C7-T1 interspace in center 
(shows upper thoracic because it tends to be very dense)

Notes: The swimmer’s technique is performed when shoulder superimposition obscures C7 on a lateral cervical spine projection or when a lateral projection of the upper thoracic vertebra is needed.

entries.title: T-Spine: LATERAL
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 48” or greater to reduce magnification 
CR: ⟂ to posterior half of thorax at T7 (if spine is horizontal)
       10-15° cephalad if spine is not horizontal
Breath: Breathing normal or Suspend at full expiration or Breathing technique (an increase        exposure time, 2-3 seconds with corresponding decrease in mA)

Collimation: 7x17
Top of IR: 1.5-2” above relaxed shoulders 

Position: 

Long axis of vertebral column aligned horizontal (Firm support for head and lower portion, if needed)
Superimpose hips and knees for true lateral position 
Center the posterior half of the thorax to the midline of the grid and at the level of T7

Adjust arms to right angle from body
Place a sheet of lead on the table, behind the patient (Absorbs scatter radiation; Prevents table scatter from affecting the image)

(Shows intervertebral foramina of the thoracic spine)

Notes: T1 to T3 are not well seen. SI of the shoulders on the upper vertebrae may cause underexposure in this area. The number of vertebrae visualized depends on the size and shape of the patient.

entries.title: C-Spine: AP AXIAL
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: 15-20° cephalic; MSP at C4 
(Enters at or slightly below Adam’s apple)
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 10” LW & 1” outside skin line on sides
IR: Top of ears

Position: 

Extend chin so occlusal plane is ⟂ to IR
C4 in center of IR
(Shows C3–T2 bodies & open intervertebral disk spaces)

Notes: Provide support for the head of any patient who has a pronounced lordotic curvature. (Helps compensate for the curvature and reduces image distortion)

entries.title: CHEST: AP (Supine)
entries.notes:
14x17  LW      SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to long axis of sternum; ⟂ to center of IR; 
        3” below jugular notch
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

Top of IR: 1.5-2” above relaxed shoulders
Collimation: 14x17

Position: 
Flex elbows; pronate hands; Place hands on hips to draw scapula laterally

Elevate head with support sponge

entries.title: CHEST: AP AXIAL - Lordotic (LINDBLOM)
entries.notes:
14x17  LW      SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to center of IR; Enters MSP at midsternum 3-4” below jugular notch
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

Top of IR: 3” above shoulders
Collimation: 14x17

Position: 

Approximately 1ft in front of grid 
Assist patient to lean backward until shoulders rest on grid

Coronal plane of thorax 15-20° from the vertical

Notes: Can do CR 15-20° when patient can’t lean back. Used to see masses or tumors.

entries.title: CHEST: MOBILE AP
entries.notes:
14x17  LW      SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to long axis of sternum; ⟂ to center of IR; 
        3” below jugular notch at T7
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration 
(if respiration assistance is provided, watch pt chest to determine inspiratory phase)

Top of IR: 1.5- 2” above shoulders
Collimation: 14x17

Position: 

Seated upright, semi upright, or supine
Greatest upright angle the patient can tolerate, whenever possible. 
Use the supine position for critically ill or injured patients 
Center MSP to IR

Internally rotate patient’s arms (if not contraindicated)
No leaning or rotation of upper torso

entries.title: SOFT TISSUE NECK: AP UPPER AIRWAY
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ through the MSP at laryngeal prominence C4 (for upper airway)
       or manubrium (for larynx and superior mediastinum)
Breath: slow inspiration 

Collimation: 12” long; 1” beyond the skin line on the sides, but not more than 10”

Position: 
Extend the patient’s neck slightly and adjust it so that the midsagittal plane is ⟂ to the plane of the IR

Notes: Used to evaluate the cervical spine or the soft tissues of the anterior neck.

entries.title: SOFT TISSUE NECK: LATERAL AP UPPER AIRWAY
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: 
Upper Airway: Horizontal through the MCP at laryngeal prominence C4  
Trachea and superior mediastinum: Level of the jugular notch halfway between the jugular notch and the MCP

Breath: slow inspiration 

Collimation: 12” long; 1” beyond the skin line on the sides, but not more than 10”

Position: 

Adjust position to center the airway to the midline of the IR
Clasp hands behind the body
Rotate the shoulders posteriorly as far as possible
Extend the patient’s neck slightly

Notes: Used to show retrosternal extensions of the thyroid gland, thymic enlargement in infants (in the recumbent position), the opacified pharynx and upper esophagus, and an outline of the trachea and bronchi. 

It is also used to locate foreign bodies.

entries.title: RIBS: PA
entries.notes:
14x17  LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to center of IR at T7; 
        To demonstrate 7th, 8th,  9th ribs - angle x-ray tube 10-15° caudad
Breath: Suspend at end of full inspiration to depress the diaphragm as much as possible

Top of IR: 1.5” above the upper border of the shoulders 
Collimation: Bilateral: 14x17
	               Unilateral: 1” beyond MSP & lateral border of the side of interest

Position: 

For unilateral ribs: center the affected side on a longitudinal plane drawn midway between the MSP and the lateral surface to grid.
Rest hands against the hips, palms out (to rotate the scapulae away from the rib cage), elbows flexed, and hands by the head on the table

If the patient is prone, rest the head on the chin or forehead and adjust the MSP to vertical 

Notes: For hypersthenic patients with wide rib cages, it may be necessary to move the patient laterally to include the entire lateral surface of the affected rib area on the radiograph.

entries.title: RIBS: AP (Posterior Ribs) below diaphragm
entries.notes:
14x17  CW     SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR at level T7  
Breath: Suspend at full expiration to elevate the diaphragm

IR: Crosswise with lower edge near level of iliac crests; 

Centered to a point halfway between xiphoid process and lower rib margin (ensures inclusion of  lower ribs b/c of divergence)

Collimation: Bilateral: ⟂ to MSP and centered to the IR
	               Unilateral: ⟂ to IR entering halfway between xiphoid and lower rib margin

Position:  

Supine recommended for lower ribs to allow gravity to move the diaphragm
Arms in a comfortable position

entries.title: RIBS: AP (Upper Anterior) above diaphragm
entries.notes:
14x17  CW or LW     SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR at level T7  
Breath: Suspend at full inspiration to depress the diaphragm

Top of IR: 1.5” above the upper border of relaxed shoulders
Collimation: Bilateral: 14x17
	               Unilateral: 1” beyond MSP & lateral border of the side of interest

Position: 

Rest hands on hips (this position moves the scapula of the ribs) 
Or extend arms, flex elbows, & rest hands under head

Shoulders in same transverse plane & rotated forward

entries.title: RIBS: AP OBLIQUE (LPO/RPO)
entries.notes:
14x17  LW     SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR at level T7  
Breath: Upper ribs: Suspend at end of full inspiration
              Lower ribs: Suspend at end of full expiration

Top of IR: 
Upper Ribs: 1.5” above the upper border of relaxed shoulders
Lower Ribs: Center to halfway between the xiphoid process and the lower rib margin

Collimation: Bilateral: 14x17
	               Unilateral: 1” beyond MSP & lateral border of the side of interest

Position: 

Oblique patient 45° RPO or LPO
Affected side down (closer) to IR
Center affected side on a longitudinal plane
halfway between MSP and lateral surface of body

Abduct and elevate arm of affected side; Rest hand on head (upright)
Place hand under or above head (recumbent)

Abduct opposite limb and rest hand on hip

Notes: AP Axillary portion of ribs on LEFT side free of SI of T-spine = LPO                   
            AP Axillary ribs Right side = LAO
entries.notesHtml:
14x17 LW SID: 40"
CR: ⟂ to IR at level T7
Breath: Upper ribs: Suspend at end of full inspiration Lower ribs: Suspend at end of full expiration
Top of IR:
  • Upper Ribs: 1.5” above the upper border of relaxed shoulders
  • Lower Ribs: Center to halfway between the xiphoid process and the lower rib margin

Collimation: Bilateral: 14x17
Unilateral: 1” beyond MSP & lateral border of the side of interest

Position:
  • Oblique patient 45° RPO or LPO
  • Affected side down (closer) to IR
  • Center affected side on a longitudinal plane halfway between MSP and lateral surface of body
  • Abduct and elevate arm of affected side; Rest hand on head (upright) Place hand under or above head (recumbent)
  • Abduct opposite limb and rest hand on hip

Notes: AP Axillary portion of ribs on LEFT side free of SI of T-spine = LPO
AP Axillary ribs Right side = LAO

entries.title: STERNUM: LATERAL
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" (to reduce magnification and distortion of the sternum)  
CR: ⟂ to IR; entering lateral border of midsternum
        CR enters elevated side of the posterior thorax at T7 and 1” lateral to MSP to elevated side
Breath: Suspend at inspiration

Collimation: 10 X 12

Position Upright: 
Rotate the shoulders posteriorly, lock hands behind back
Keep MSP of body vertical, rest shoulders against grid
Large breasts drawn to sides, held in position with wide bandage so shadows don’t obscure lower position of sternum

Position Recumbent:

Dorsal decubitus may be used for patient condition

Extend arms over head to prevent overlapping sternum

Rest head on the arms or on a pillow

Place support under lower thoracic region (to position long axis of sternum horizontally)

Notes: Sternum in its entirety (from jugular notch to tip of xiphoid)

entries.title: STERNUM: PA OBLIQUE (RAO)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 30"  
CR: ⟂ to IR;
        CR enters elevated side of the posterior thorax at T7 and 1” lateral to MSP to elevated side
Breath: Breathing technique - slow, shallow breaths during long exposure

OR full expiration; 
When a short exposure time is to be used, instruct the patient to suspend breathing at the end of expiration to minimize the visibility of the pulmonary vasculature 


Top of IR: Top of IR 1.5” above jugular notch (to get full sternum)
Collimation: 10 X 12

Position: 

Rotate 15-20° in RAO recumbent (to use the heart for contrast)
If recumbent, have patient support body on forearm and flexed knee
Ensure left shoulder and hip rotated equal amount (to prevent superimposition of the vertebrae & sternum)
Long axis of sternum aligned to midline of grid


Notes: Trauma patients unable to lie prone: use LPO in AP oblique projection;
Deep chest = less of an angle; RAO position best demonstrates sternum over the heart

entries.title: SC JOINTS: PA
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to center of IR; MSP at T3; C7 (vertebral prominence)
      Breath: Suspend at end of expiration 

Top of IR: At jugular notch, then turn patient around	
Collimation: 6x8

Position: 
Place arms along sides of body, palms facing upward
Bilateral: Rest head on chin; MSP should be vertical

Unilateral: Turn head to face affected side & rest cheek on table (provides better visualization of the lateral portion of the manubrium)

Exposure field centered to level of spinous process of 3rd thoracic vertebra (posterior to jugular notch)

Chin on bucky
Turn head right to see right SC joints
Turn head left to see left SC joints


Notes: SC joints are at T3 or T4

entries.title: SC JOINTS: PA OBLIQUE (RAO/LAO)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to SC joint closest to IR (at T2-T3); 
       CR enters 3" below the vertebral prominens;
       1-2" lateral to the MSP on the elevated side
      Breath: Suspend at expiration 

Top of IR: At jugular notch, then turn patient around	
Collimation: 6x8

Position: 

Rotate the patient 10-15° affected side down (vertebrae should be well behind the SC joint closest to IR)
Turn head right to see right SC joints
Turn head left to see left SC joints
Turn head to the side

entries.title: ABDOMEN: AP SUPINE (KUB) *preferred
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; MSP at level of iliac crests
Breath: Suspend on expiration 

Collimation: 14x17
IR: Centered to iliac crests; Include pubis symphysis, don’t clip!

Position: 

Supine, without rotation (preferred over upright)
Support knees to reduce strain
For tall patients, obtain a second image for bladder 

Notes: Hypersthenic patients may require 2 crosswise projections;
Tall patients may require separate bladder image (upper & lower)

entries.title: ABDOMEN: LATERAL DECUBITUS
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to GRID
Breath: Suspend at end of full expiration (Taken 5 minutes after patient lies on their side when free intraperitoneal air is suspected. Allows air to rise to its highest level within the abdomen)
 
Collimation: 14x17
IR: Centered to iliac crests or 2" above (if diaphragm is to be demonstrated)

Position: 

Left lateral recumbent position (mostly performed)
Elevate patient 2-3” with sponge
Arms above the level of the diaphragm
Flex knees slightly to provide stabilization

Notes: For patients too ill to stand; Side down for fluid, side up for free air;
When looking for free air, choose Left Lateral Decubitus (no right decubitus b/c air is in the stomach)

entries.title: ABDOMEN: DORSAL DECUBITUS
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to GRID; MCP 2” above iliac crests
Breath: Suspend at end of full expiration 
 
Collimation: 14x17
IR: Centered to iliac crests or 2" above (if diaphragm is to be demonstrated)

Position: 

Supine (right or left side in contact with vertical grid device)
Arms crossed on upper chest or behind head
Vertical grid device aligned to the long axis of IR with MCP
Vertical grid centered to the MCP 2” above iliac crests to IR

Notes:  For patients who can’t stand or lie on their side (for free air)

entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: Hor. and ⟂ to MSP;  2” above level of iliac crests (to include diaphragm)

IR: Centered to iliac crests; Include pubis symphysis, don’t clip!

Arms out of radiation field

Tall patients may require separate bladder image (upper & lower)
